summary: 62 messages (26 Sarah, 36 ALTR, 1 silent membership event). THE DEFINING FACT OF THIS WINDOW: in seven days this client handed five separate live credentials into a group chat that contains outsourced vendor accounts, and every single one of them was asked for by ALTR. On 09-11 she posted her Snapchat login in plaintext — '@sarahxlloyd\n[REDACTED-PASSWORD]' — after Mayson asked 'did you get the password?'. On 09-16 Mayson asked 'Are you able to give us login for one of them?' about her Facebook accounts. On 09-17 she posted a screenshot of her Facebook details ('Here are Facebook details') and her personal mobile number ('Maybe try +[REDACTED-NUMBER]'). Vivek asked for a second set the same day ('Okay share the details'). Then on 09-17 at 14:51 and 09-18 at 01:30 Mayson asked for live Snapchat 2FA codes and she sent them — '[REDACTED-2FA-CODE]' and '[REDACTED-2FA-CODE]'. The timing is the part that should stop the room: at 11:03 on 09-17, Mica posted a formal security advisory into this exact chat that ends 'Please do not send your backup codes to anyone, including our team. Keep the screenshot somewhere secure that only you can access.' Three hours and forty-eight minutes later one of our own people asked her for a code, and she sent it. This is twenty days after her main Instagram was confirmed hacked, and fifty-one days after the Facebook password she pasted here on 2026-07-29 at Vivek's request — still never rotated. Her new Snapchat password '[REDACTED-PASSWORD]' is built on the same template as the un-rotated '[REDACTED-PASSWORD]'. Two more members were silently added to this group (09-10 20:03, and 09-17 22:03 — five hours after the first 2FA code was posted), making six unexplained membership changes in four weeks. THE PAYMENT MYSTERY RESOLVED — AND IT RESOLVED BADLY. Last week's report flagged that the Aug 15-31 invoice had sailed past its due date with nobody on either side saying a word. It had in fact been paid, and OVERPAID. We only know because of a parenthetical in the next invoice: on 09-15 Stephski wrote 'Noting I have deducted the overpayment from last period from this invoice'. She was never told 'Received!'. That is the second overpayment in three months (the July 1-15 overpayment was $3,538) on a client who has audited five consecutive invoices and been right every time. Worse, the same message moves her OFF the only account that works: 'It's very important that you send to the ALTR Management account listed at the bottom of this invoice, vs the one you sent to last period' — twelve days after Stephski told her to keep using the ALTR Platform Services LLC account ending 4709. That is the fourth change to our receiving details in ten weeks, and the last one cost two bounced wires and four days of lateness. And for the first time in this account's history the invoice carried a consequence: 'we appreciate you paying within the next 7 days to avoid any pausing in work!' — sent to a client whose every late payment on record was caused by us. She replied within 37 minutes of being chased: 'Hey, thankyou! Will get this paid today :)'. THE MOST RELIABLE SERVICE ON THE ACCOUNT STOPPED. Michelle's weekly DMCA leak-removal report had landed every week without fail since 2026-07-10 (07-10, 07-17, 07-26, 08-01, 08-10, 08-17, 08-25, 09-01, 09-08). The 09-15 slot passed with nothing. Michelle wrote zero messages this window. Sarah did not chase — she has never had to. THE STALE STACK DID NOT MOVE, AGAIN. Noah wrote 0 messages (last post 2026-08-25, 24 days), Ronnie 0 (last 08-26, 23 days), Derrek 0 (last 08-25, 24 days), and the vendor 'Sarah Lloyd chat team' 0 (last 2026-06-15, 95 days). The sexting-set request is now 97 days old and has never once been answered by any human. The 9am AEST good-morning on her $25k whale is 96 days old with still no named chatter. She has now gone 24 days without mentioning her biggest whale and THREE consecutive reporting periods without raising a single service complaint. The Monday trial-reels call Mayson proposed on 09-04 is 14 days dead and has never been mentioned again. SHE EXPLAINED THE CONTENT MISS AND NOBODY LISTENED. On 09-16, replying to Michelle's 09-10 chase, she wrote 'And sorry I'll try upload this week. I do have a full time assistant who uploads across all of my accounts so just can be hard trying to find things that she hasn't already uploaded'. That is a structural blocker against a brief that demands content which 'has to be fresh' and 'If it's already posted on your main account, it doesn't count'. Mayson's entire reply was 'No worries'. Nineteen days after the brief, nothing has been uploaded and nobody has solved the actual problem. SHE ALSO OPENED A NEW META TICKET AND GOT NOTHING: on 09-17, 'I have another Facebook as well that's down at the moment if I can please have your help @fonta I'll be home in an hour and will send details'. Vivek: 'Okay share the details', then 'No problem'. Nothing since. Against all of that: she is still warm, fast and completely without friction — 26 messages in seven days, not one sharp word, 'Ok easy, I'll get log in info tomorrow :)', 'Yes! Lmk when you need a new one'. Of the 36 messages ALTR sent her this week, 24 were Mayson, and almost every one of them was an ask.

health.rationale: Down 6 from 32. One genuine relief and three genuine deteriorations. The relief: last week's worst open question — had the Aug 15-31 invoice been collected — is answered, and it was paid. But it resolved into something worse than the uncertainty. She had overpaid (the second uncaught overpayment in three months), nobody ever confirmed receipt to her, and we only learned it ourselves from a parenthetical in the following invoice. The deteriorations. FIRST AND DOMINANT: the security posture did not just fail to improve, it got materially worse and we caused it. Five live credential disclosures into a group chat containing outsourced vendor accounts in seven days — a Snapchat password, a Facebook credential screenshot, her personal mobile number, and two live 2FA codes — every one of them solicited by ALTR, twenty days after her main Instagram was confirmed hacked and fifty-one days after the Facebook password she posted here on 2026-07-29 that has still never been rotated. The aggravating detail is that our own Social Media Director posted a formal advisory in this chat at 11:03 on 09-17 saying 'Please do not send your backup codes to anyone, including our team', and Mayson asked her for one at 14:51 the same day. Two further unexplained members were added to the group, one of them five hours after a 2FA code was posted. SECOND: billing hygiene regressed. A fourth change of receiving account in ten weeks, moving her off the only account her bank has accepted, twelve days after being told to stay on it — the exact configuration that produced two bounced wires and four days of lateness last month — and the first payment-pause threat in the account's history, aimed at the only party in this relationship that has never been the cause of a delay. THIRD: Michelle's weekly DMCA report, unbroken for ten weeks and repeatedly named in these reports as the single most reliable service on the account, was missed. When the one thing that always works stops working, there is nothing left on the delivery side to point at. Underneath it all the stale stack simply aged another seven days with zero movement: sexting sets 97 days and never once answered by any human, the whale good-morning 96, chatting-quality verdict 83, MM repetition 84, Meta explanation 41, Phone Farm 48, chargebacks 30, the Aug 25 call write-up 24, the Aug 24 screenshots 25. Noah, Ronnie, Derrek and the entire vendor chat team wrote nothing for the fourth consecutive week. She raised no service complaint for the third consecutive period and has not mentioned her $25k whale in 24 days. The score is not lower only because she is still personally warm and instantly responsive, because the Sept 1-14 invoice went out on time with the overpayment proactively credited rather than making her ask, because Stephski pre-warned her to withdraw from OF before invoicing, and because Mica did two genuinely good things this week — resuming weekly reel inspo and writing the security advisory that the rest of us then ignored. The gap between how cooperative she remains and what she is actually receiving is now the whole risk on this account.
